title: Filters, cross filters, row-level formulas, summary formulas, and bucketing
objectives: Choose a field filter, filter logic, or a cross filter when the question is about related records WITH or WITHOUT a child.
Contrast row-level formulas (each record) with summary formulas (groups and totals).
Use bucketing to categorize numeric, picklist, or text values inside one report.
Cite Help limits: 20 field filters, 5 formulas, 3 cross filters, 5 bucket fields.
diagnostic_question: A manager wants Accounts without open Cases, a per-row age column, a win-rate on each Stage group, and deal sizes of Small/Medium/Large—without new custom fields. Which report tools do you stack, and which do you refuse?
definition: After report type and format, you shape results with field filters (up to 20), optional filter logic, cross filters on related objects (up to 3, with up to 5 subfilters each), row-level formulas that evaluate each record, summary formulas that evaluate groups and totals, and bucket columns that categorize values in that report only. ([Limits](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=analytics.rd_reports_dashboards_limits.htm); [Add a Bucket Column](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=analytics.reports_bucketing_adding.htm))
why_it_matters: Interviewers listen for WITH/WITHOUT related records (cross filter) versus a custom report type relationship (ANA-001), and for row-level versus summary formulas. Buckets are report-local. Limits are Help facts: filter logic does not apply to cross filters.
sixty_second_explanation: Think of an airport checkpoint. Field filters are the boarding-pass scan. Cross filters ask whether you have a connecting bag (WITH) or none (WITHOUT). A row-level formula weighs each suitcase. A summary formula weighs the whole flight or gate group. Bucketing sorts bags into Small/Medium/Large bins on this flight only—not a new permanent tag in the cargo system.
deeper_explanation: Field filters per report are allocated at 20 in the report builder (10 if someone still uses the old wizard). Some date-range filters consume multiple custom filters toward that 20. Filter logic applies only to field filters, not to cross filters. ([Reports and Dashboards Limits](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=analytics.rd_reports_dashboards_limits.htm))

Cross filters filter across objects: each report can have up to 3 cross filters, each with up to 5 subfilters. They are the report-level WITH/WITHOUT related-record tool. They are not supported on reports that include external objects.

Formulas per report are allocated at 5. Row-level formulas evaluate each record and appear as a column you can edit in Lightning. Summary formulas evaluate groups and totals; PARENTGROUPVAL and PREVGROUPVAL are available with summary, matrix, and joined reports. ([Formula Operators and Functions](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.customize_functions.htm); [Edit a Row-Level Formula](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=analytics.reports_formulas_row_level_edit.htm))

Bucket columns categorize numeric, picklist, or text values. Each report can include up to 5 bucket fields; each bucket field up to 20 buckets; each bucket up to 20 values. Buckets exist only in that report unless you instead create an object formula field. ([Add a Bucket Column](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=analytics.reports_bucketing_adding.htm))
These features are report metadata. They do not insert business records. They also do not replace sharing: a filter cannot show a row the user is not allowed to see.

mental_model.analogy: An airport checkpoint: scans (filters), connecting-bag checks (cross filters), per-suitcase scales (row-level formulas), per-flight scales (summary formulas), and size bins used only on this flight (buckets).
useful_mapping: filter logic → AND/OR among scans, not among bag checks
cross filter WITH → must have a connecting bag
cross filter WITHOUT → must have no connecting bag
summary formula → weigh the flight or gate group
bucket column → Small/Medium/Large bins on this flight only
object formula field → a permanent cargo tag used by every flight
where_it_breaks: Airports do not have a 20-filter allocation.
Cross filters are not the same as a custom report type inner/outer relationship.
Sharing can hide a bag the checkpoint never sees.

teach_back_prompt: Explain field filters versus cross filters versus row-level versus summary formulas versus bucketing using the airport checkpoint, then name one Help limit and one place the analogy breaks.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: Field filters cut by values. Cross filters ask WITH or WITHOUT a related record. Row-level formulas calculate each row. Summary formulas calculate groups. Buckets categorize values in this report only. Logic does not apply to cross filters.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I stack tools after type and format. Accounts without Cases is a WITHOUT cross filter, not a CRT rebuild, unless the type cannot see Case. Age of each Opportunity is a row-level formula. Win rate by Stage is a summary formula, maybe PARENTGROUPVAL. Deal size Small/Medium/Large is a numeric bucket if we do not need a durable field. I stay inside 20 field filters, 3 cross filters, 5 formulas, and 5 bucket fields. I never claim a filter bypasses sharing.

terminology.plain: A condition on a field already on the report type, such as Stage equals Closed Won.
terminology.precise: Up to 20 in the report builder. Some date ranges consume multiple filters. Filter logic applies to these, not to cross filters.
terminology.example: Close Date equals This Fiscal Quarter AND Amount greater than 0.
terminology.non_example: A cross filter 'Accounts without Cases' is not a field filter.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: List view filter: similar idea, different metadata.
terminology.boundary: You cannot filter reports by custom long text area fields per the limits article.

terminology.precise: Applies only to field filters. If you apply filter logic to a locked filter, the lock is removed.
terminology.example: (1 AND 2) OR 3 on Stage, Amount, and Type.
terminology.non_example: Trying to OR two cross filters together with the same logic box.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Cross filter subfilters: up to 5 per cross filter, not the field-filter logic box.
terminology.boundary: Locked-filter plus logic interaction is in the limits article.

terminology.plain: A report filter that keeps rows WITH or WITHOUT related records of another object.
terminology.precise: Up to 3 per report, 5 subfilters each. Not supported with external objects. Filter logic does not apply to them.
terminology.example: Accounts WITHOUT Cases, subfilter Status equals Open.
terminology.non_example: A custom report type set to must-have related Cases (that is ANA-001).
terminology.boundary: Use when the type already includes the parent; you are filtering related presence, not defining the type.

terminology.plain: A calculation that runs once per report row and shows as a column.
terminology.precise: Edited in Lightning from the formula column. Evaluates each record. Counts toward formulas-per-report allocation.
terminology.example: Close Date minus Created Date as Time to Close on each Opportunity.
terminology.non_example: PARENTGROUPVAL, which is a summary function, not a per-row field formula.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Object formula field: stored on every record and reusable everywhere.
terminology.boundary: Permissions differ for private versus public reports.

terminology.plain: A calculation on a grouping or grand total, not on each detail row.
terminology.precise: Used on summary, matrix, and joined reports. PARENTGROUPVAL returns a parent grouping value; PREVGROUPVAL returns a previous grouping.
terminology.example: Won Amount / PARENTGROUPVAL(Amount) as a win rate within Stage.
terminology.boundary: Joined reports have extra custom-summary-formula caps in the limits article.

terminology.plain: A summary function that reads the total from a grouping above the current one.
terminology.precise: Available in custom summary formulas at grouping levels, not at summary levels, on summary, matrix, and joined reports.
terminology.example: Region amount as a percent of the country parent group.
terminology.non_example: A row-level formula referencing another row's Amount.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: PREVGROUPVAL: previous peer grouping, increment up to 12.
terminology.boundary: Do not invent other PARENT* functions.

terminology.plain: A report-only grouping of values into named bins.
terminology.precise: Numeric, picklist, or text. Max 5 bucket fields, 20 buckets, 20 values each. Not on external-object reports. Not reused on other reports.
terminology.non_example: A picklist field on the object used by every report and list view.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Report grouping: you can group by a bucket once it exists.
terminology.boundary: Filtering a bucket drops custom-index gains on the source field.

terminology.plain: An extra condition on the related object inside a cross filter.
terminology.precise: Up to 5 subfilters per cross filter.
terminology.example: WITHOUT Cases where Status equals Open and Origin equals Phone.
terminology.non_example: A fourth cross filter (the cap is 3 cross filters).
terminology.boundary: Subfilters do not get the field-filter logic box.

when_to_use: When a field filter or filter logic can cut the result set without changing the report type.
When the question is Accounts WITH or WITHOUT related Cases—use a cross filter rather than a new object.
When each row needs a calculation (row-level formula) or each group needs a ratio (summary formula).
When you need Small/Medium/Large bucketing on this report only, without a new custom field.
when_not_to_use: Do not use a cross filter to add an object the report type cannot see; fix the custom report type first (ANA-001).
Do not use bucketing as a company-wide picklist replacement when many reports and list views need the same bins.
Do not put PARENTGROUPVAL in a row-level formula or on a tabular report that has no groupings.
Do not use filters, formulas, or buckets to bypass sharing, FLS, or the 2,000-row display cap (ANA-005).
configuration_or_code_location: Lightning report builder: Filters pane; cross filter controls; Columns → row-level formula; summary formula on groupings; Bucket This Column.
Object Manager formula field if the calculation must be reused outside this report.

decision_table.signal: Need rows where a field on the same report type matches a value or date range.
decision_table.choose: Field filter, then filter logic if you need AND/OR among those filters.
decision_table.not: A cross filter on that same field.
decision_table.why: Cross filters answer related-record presence, not ordinary field values.

decision_table.signal: Need Accounts that have no open Cases, or Opportunities with at least one Product.
decision_table.choose: Cross filter WITHOUT or WITH, plus subfilters (max 3 / 5).
decision_table.not: A new custom report type unless the type cannot see the related object.
decision_table.why: Help positions cross filters as filter-across-objects; CRT is the type graph.

decision_table.signal: Need a number that is different on every detail row, such as age in days.
decision_table.not: PARENTGROUPVAL or a summary formula at the detail grain.
decision_table.why: Row-level formulas evaluate each record; summary functions evaluate groups.

decision_table.signal: Need a ratio or comparison at Stage or Owner totals.
decision_table.choose: Summary formula, using PARENTGROUPVAL or PREVGROUPVAL when the functions Help allows.
decision_table.why: Summary functions exist for grouped formats, not as picklist bins.

decision_table.signal: Need Small/Medium/Large on this report only, without a new custom field.
decision_table.choose: Numeric bucket column (max 5 bucket fields on the report).
decision_table.not: A durable object formula if only one report will ever need the bins.
decision_table.why: Buckets are report-local; object fields are for reuse across reports and lists.

limitations: Filter logic does not apply to cross filters.
Buckets, cross filters, and row-level formulas are unavailable on reports that include external objects (limits article).
Five formulas per report; joined reports have additional custom-summary-formula caps.
Does not replace dashboard filters (ANA-004) or sharing diagnosis (ANA-005).
security_notes: Filters cannot reveal rows the user cannot see.
A row-level formula on a sensitive field still requires FLS to the inputs.
Do not email filtered reports of real customers as a lab artifact.
common_mistakes: Using filter logic on cross filters.
Rebuilding a CRT for a WITHOUT question.
Putting PARENTGROUPVAL in a row-level formula.
Expecting buckets to travel to other reports.

interview_questions.question: How do you choose among filters, cross filters, row-level formulas, summary formulas, and bucketing?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Field filters cut values. Cross filters ask WITH or WITHOUT a related record. Row-level formulas calculate each row. Summary formulas calculate groups. Buckets categorize values on this report only.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I start from grain. If the type already has the field, I filter it—max 20, logic only on those filters. If the question is related presence, I use a cross filter (max 3) rather than rebuilding a CRT. Age-style math is row-level. Win-rate-style math is a summary formula with PARENTGROUPVAL when Help allows. Small/Medium/Large is a bucket if we do not need reuse; otherwise an object field. I stay inside the 5-formula and 5-bucket caps.
interview_questions.example: Quarter filter + WITHOUT open Cases + age column + Stage win rate + Amount buckets on one summary report.
follow_ups: Does logic apply to cross filters?

interview_questions.question: What is a cross filter, and when is it the wrong tool?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: A cross filter keeps parent rows WITH or WITHOUT related children, with up to five subfilters. It is wrong when the report type cannot see that child—then you need a custom report type.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I describe WITH and WITHOUT as report-level related presence. I cite 3 cross filters and 5 subfilters, and I say filter logic will not combine them. I contrast ANA-001: must-have on a CRT changes every report of that type. I refuse cross filters on external-object reports because Help lists them as unsupported. I do not use a cross filter to calculate age or win rate.
interview_questions.example: Accounts WITHOUT Cases, subfilter Status equals Open.
tradeoffs: One report's cross filter vs a CRT change
Subfilters vs a second cross filter
follow_ups: Can you OR two cross filters in the logic box?
What if Case is not on the type?
weak_answer_warnings: Calling a CRT a cross filter

interview_questions.question: Build 'this quarter's deals without open cases, with age, win rate, and size bins' in words.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Field filter on Close Date, WITHOUT Cases cross filter, row-level age, summary win rate on a grouped format, numeric Amount buckets. No new production fields required.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I pick a summary Opportunities report grouped by Stage so summary formulas have a home. Close Date is a field filter. Open-case absence is a cross filter with a Status subfilter. Age is row-level. Win rate uses a summary formula, possibly PARENTGROUPVAL. Size is a three-range numeric bucket. I count toward 20/3/5/5. I verify with a LAB Opportunity that has an open case versus one that does not. I warn buckets will not appear on the next report.
interview_questions.example: The worked example LAB report in a sandbox.
tradeoffs: Summary format vs matrix for win rate
follow_ups: What if they need the bins on a list view?
What if formulas already equal five?

interview_questions.question: A developer wants to add PARENTGROUPVAL to a tabular phone list. How do you respond?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: PARENTGROUPVAL is a summary function for summary, matrix, and joined reports at grouping levels. A tabular list has no parent group. Use a row-level formula or change format.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I open the functions Help mentally: summary functions are not for tabular grain. If they need a per-row calculation, that is a row-level formula. If they need a percent of a group, they must group first—summary or matrix. I will not 'hack' PARENTGROUPVAL into a list. I also keep them inside five formulas and remind them this is report metadata, not a new Opportunity field.
interview_questions.example: Phone list stays tabular; a separate summary report holds win rate by owner.
weak_answer_warnings: Confusing summary format with summary formula

interview_questions.question: Users added filter logic and the WITHOUT Cases clause seems ignored. What do you check?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Filter logic does not apply to cross filters. The WITHOUT clause still runs independently. I check they did not hit the 3-cross-filter cap or lose the type relationship.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I look at the Filters pane and separate field filters from the cross filter. I explain Help's sentence: logic is for field filters only. If they tried to OR a Stage filter with WITHOUT Cases inside the logic box, that OR never bound the cross filter. I may add a field filter they actually need, or I accept that WITH/WITHOUT is always on. I also confirm this is not an outer CRT filter trap from ANA-001.
interview_questions.example: Logic '(1 OR 2)' on Stage and Amount; WITHOUT Cases still applied to every row.
tradeoffs: Two reports vs one confusing filter stack
CRT inner join vs cross filter
weak_answer_warnings: Rewriting logic five times without naming the Help rule

interview_questions.question: A bucket used for grouping vanished after someone edited bucket values. What else might have happened?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Help says if a bucket column has a filter, modifying bucket values removes filters that refer to that column. The bucket is also report-local, so another report never had it.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I check whether a filter referenced the bucket—editing values drops those filters. I recreate the filter. I explain 5/20/20 caps if they cannot add another bucket. I ask whether they expected org-wide reuse; if yes, we promote an object field. I mention custom-index loss if they filter the bucket. I do not treat this as a sharing bug.
interview_questions.example: Medium bucket renamed; the filter 'Bucket equals Medium' disappeared.
tradeoffs: Recreate filter vs promote to a field
weak_answer_warnings: Assuming a release deleted buckets org-wide

interview_questions.question: When do you refuse a report formula and ask for an object field instead?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: When many reports, list views, validation, or automation need the same calculation or bins. Report formulas and buckets are local and capped at five formulas and five bucket fields.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I keep report formulas for interview-friendly, report-only math. Age used in one forecast report can be row-level. Age used in assignment rules cannot. Small/Medium/Large used in ten dashboards should be a field. I also refuse formulas as a way to dodge FLS or to stitch unrelated objects. If we are already at five formulas, I split reports or move logic to the object. I stay out of CRM Analytics unless the grain truly leaves core reports (ANA-006).
interview_questions.example: Deal-size bins needed on list views and two dozen reports: picklist or formula field, not 24 buckets.
tradeoffs: Deployment of a field vs report-only speed
follow_ups: When is a CRT the better change?

interview_questions.question: Teach this topic with the airport checkpoint and then break the analogy.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Scans are field filters, connecting bags are cross filters, suitcase scales are row-level, flight scales are summary, size bins are buckets. The analogy breaks because logic does not apply to bag checks and because sharing hides bags the checkpoint never sees.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I map each Help limit onto the picture: 20 scans, 3 bag checks, 5 suitcase formulas, 5 bin fields. I say PARENTGROUPVAL is a gate-group scale, not a suitcase scale. I refuse a library story. I warn that external-object flights cannot use bags, bins, or suitcase formulas. I finish with WITH/WITHOUT versus CRT must-have so the interviewer hears two layers.
interview_questions.example: Whiteboard the checkpoint, then write 20 / 3 / 5 / 5 under it.
follow_ups: Where does the checkpoint analogy break?
